name: Hot Big Bang
origin_source: Lemaitre 1927/1931 (Ann. Soc. Sci. Bruxelles; Nature 127:706); Gamow, Alpher, Herman 1948
core_idea: The universe expanded from a hot, dense state about 13.8 billion years ago; it is a model of evolution, not of a moment of creation.
status: Established: CMB, light-element abundances, Hubble expansion. What 'came before' is outside the model.
proposal: Dome law: the creature can measure its dome's own 'redshift' (expansion of its arena) and infer a beginning.

name: Cosmic inflation
origin_source: Guth 1981 (Phys. Rev. D 23:347); Linde 1982; Albrecht and Steinhardt 1982; Starobinsky 1980
core_idea: A brief burst of exponential expansion flattened and smoothed the early universe and seeded structure from quantum fluctuations.
status: Leading paradigm; predicted near-scale-invariant fluctuations confirmed. Primordial B-modes not yet detected; critics (Ijjas, Steinhardt, Loeb 2017) call it unfalsifiable in its eternal form.
proposal: QWM: inflation as an 'early-training' phase where tiny noise becomes large structure, a template for latent initialization.

name: No-boundary proposal
core_idea: In quantum cosmology time becomes space-like near the start, so the universe has no boundary or first instant, like the South Pole of a sphere.
status: Serious but technically disputed (Feldbrugge, Lehners, Turok 2017 argued instability; debate continues).
proposal: Dome rule: the dome has no 'first tick'; asking 'what was before tick 0' returns a geometry error.

name: Creation from nothing by quantum tunneling
core_idea: The universe tunnelled into existence from 'nothing' (no space, time or matter), with total energy possibly zero.
status: Serious speculation; critics note the 'nothing' still presupposes quantum laws.
proposal: Puzzle: the creature finds the dome's total 'energy ledger' sums to zero.

name: White holes and white-hole Big Bang
origin_source: White hole: Novikov 1964 and later; Big Bang-as-white-hole: Retter and Heller 2011 (New Astron. 17); Rovelli and Vidotto on black-to-white transitions 2014-2018
core_idea: A white hole is the time-reverse of a black hole: nothing can enter, matter only leaves. Some speculate our Big Bang was one.
status: Valid mathematical solutions of GR; never observed; thought unstable. Loop-gravity 'Planck star' variants are speculative.
proposal: Dome hazard: a 'fountain' region the creature can never enter but which spits out resources.

name: Conformal cyclic cosmology
core_idea: The infinitely expanded far future of one aeon is conformally the Big Bang of the next; the universe is an endless chain of aeons.
status: Contested; claimed 'Hawking points' in CMB (An, Meissner, Nurowski, Penrose 2020) are disputed by other analyses.
proposal: Dome rule: when the dome reaches maximum dilution it rescales and restarts; faint 'scars' of the prior aeon persist.

name: Ekpyrotic and cyclic cosmology
origin_source: Khoury, Ovrut, Steinhardt, Turok 2001 (Phys. Rev. D 64); Steinhardt and Turok 2002
core_idea: Our universe began when two branes collided in a higher dimension, and the collision may repeat in cycles.
status: Serious alternative to inflation; predicts negligible primordial gravitational waves.
proposal: Dome rule: a periodic 'collision' resets the arena; the creature could learn its period.

name: Big Bounce (loop quantum cosmology)
core_idea: Quantum geometry halts collapse at Planck density, so a prior contracting universe 'bounced' into ours.
status: Serious hypothesis inside loop quantum gravity; no direct evidence.
proposal: Dome law: density has a hard ceiling; crushing matter past it causes a rebound.

name: Oscillating universe
origin_source: Friedmann 1922 (closed solutions); Tolman 1934 'Relativity, Thermodynamics and Cosmology'
core_idea: A closed universe expands, recollapses and re-expands forever.
status: Largely abandoned: entropy grows each cycle (Tolman's own objection) and the expansion is accelerating.
proposal: Dome puzzle: each cycle the creature finds more 'disorder' carried over, a hint the cycle cannot be eternal.

name: Eternal inflation
core_idea: Inflation never stops everywhere; it keeps budding off 'pocket universes', each a separate Big Bang.
status: Follows in many inflation models; criticized for the measure problem and weak testability.
proposal: Dome design: neighbouring 'pocket domes' with different constants, discoverable only by rare collisions.

name: String landscape
origin_source: Bousso and Polchinski 2000; Kachru, Kallosh, Linde, Trivedi 2003 (KKLT); Susskind 2003
core_idea: String theory admits an enormous number of stable vacua, each with different low-energy physics.
status: Contested; the 'swampland' program (Vafa 2005; Obied et al. 2018) questions whether de Sitter vacua exist at all.
proposal: QWM: treat physical laws as one point in a landscape of possible rule-sets the model can sample.

name: Bubble-universe collisions
origin_source: Aguirre, Johnson, Shomer 2007; Feeney, Johnson, Mortlock, Peiris 2011 (PRL 107)
core_idea: If eternal inflation is true, our bubble may have collided with others, leaving circular marks on the CMB.
status: Searches in WMAP and Planck found no significant signal.
proposal: Dome puzzle: rare circular 'bruises' on the sky reveal a neighbour dome.

name: Tegmark's four multiverse levels
core_idea: A classification: I distant regions; II other inflationary bubbles; III Everett branches; IV all mathematical structures.
status: Organizing scheme; levels have very different status (Level I is near-certain given infinite space; Level IV is metaphysics).
proposal: Paper scaffold: QWM's 'world' can be scoped by level: one dome, many domes, many branches, many rule-sets.

name: Cosmological natural selection
origin_source: Smolin 1992 (Class. Quantum Grav. 9:173); 'The Life of the Cosmos' 1997
core_idea: Each black hole spawns a baby universe with slightly mutated constants, so universes that make many black holes dominate.
status: Contested; unusually for a multiverse it makes predictions (e.g. neutron-star mass limits), and 2-solar-mass pulsars (2010) put pressure on it.
proposal: Dome evolution: domes that produce more 'sinks' spawn more child domes; the creature could detect it is a descendant.

name: Black-hole cosmology
core_idea: Our observable universe might be the interior of a black hole in a larger parent universe.
status: Fringe-to-speculative; occasionally revived with claims about galaxy spin asymmetry (Shamir 2020s, disputed).
proposal: Dome reveal: the dome's edge behaves like an event horizon seen from inside.

name: Fine-tuning of the constants
origin_source: Carter 1974; Barrow and Tipler 1986; Rees 'Just Six Numbers' 1999; Hoyle 1953 carbon resonance (prediction story partly mythologized)
core_idea: Small changes in constants such as the cosmological constant or the strong-force strength would forbid complex chemistry and life.
status: The sensitivity is widely accepted for some parameters; what it means (luck, multiverse, design, deeper law) is open.
proposal: Dome tuning: let the creature explore 'nearby' parameter settings and see which ones allow it to exist.

name: Anthropic principle (weak and strong)
origin_source: Carter 1974 (IAU Symposium 63); Dicke 1961 (Nature 192:440); Barrow and Tipler 1986
core_idea: Weak: we must observe conditions compatible with observers. Strong: the universe must be such that observers arise.
status: Weak form is near-tautological but useful (Weinberg's 1987 cosmological-constant estimate). Strong and 'final' forms are contested metaphysics.
proposal: Dome inference: the creature can reason 'my dome must allow me', a first step toward suspecting design.

name: Dirac large numbers hypothesis
core_idea: Huge dimensionless ratios in physics (around 10^40) are related, so constants like G may vary with cosmic age.
status: Varying-G version excluded by observations; the coincidences are now usually explained anthropically (Dicke 1961).
proposal: Puzzle: the creature notices two huge ratios in its dome match; are they linked or coincidence?

name: Copernican / mediocrity principle
origin_source: Copernicus 1543 (De revolutionibus); principle named by Bondi 1952
core_idea: We are not in a special place; assume our situation is typical.
status: Working assumption of cosmology; in tension with anthropic selection effects and with 'Axis of Evil' claims.
proposal: Dome humility rule: the creature should assume its patch is typical until proven otherwise.

name: Boltzmann brains
origin_source: Background: Boltzmann 1895-96 fluctuation hypothesis (with Schuetz); term 'Boltzmann brain': Albrecht and Sorbo 2004 (Phys. Rev. D 70:063528)
core_idea: In an eternal universe, random fluctuations producing a lone brain with false memories vastly outnumber evolved observers, so any model predicting that is suspect.
status: Used as a reductio against cosmological models (Carroll 2017 'cognitively unstable'). Not believed to exist.
touchstones: Futurama-style jokes; Boltzmann brain episodes of many podcasts
proposal: Dome sanity check: a QWM world model that predicts its own observers are mostly noise-born should be rejected.

name: The measure problem
origin_source: Linde, Vilenkin and others 1990s-2000s; Guth 2007 'Eternal inflation and its implications'
core_idea: In an infinite multiverse, everything happens infinitely often, so probabilities need a 'measure', and results depend on that choice.
status: Recognized open problem; no agreed solution.
proposal: QWM: any infinite-branching world model needs an explicit weighting rule or its predictions are meaningless.

name: Heat death
core_idea: The universe approaches maximum entropy where no free energy is left to do work.
status: Default fate in standard cosmology with a cosmological constant (de Sitter equilibrium).
proposal: Dome law: a finite free-energy budget; long-game strategies must account for the dome running down.

name: Big Rip
core_idea: If dark energy grows stronger (w < -1), expansion eventually tears apart galaxies, planets, then atoms.
status: Possible but not favoured; 2025 DESI hints suggest dark energy may be weakening rather than strengthening.
proposal: Dome hazard: a growing repulsion that slowly breaks the arena's structures.

name: Big Crunch
core_idea: Gravity halts expansion and the universe collapses back to a singularity.
status: Disfavoured by accelerated expansion, though evolving dark energy could in principle reopen it.
proposal: Dome finale: if the dome contracts, the end-game is to squeeze computation out of collapse (Tipler-style).

name: False vacuum decay
origin_source: Coleman 1977 (Phys. Rev. D 15:2929); Coleman and De Luccia 1980
core_idea: Our vacuum might not be the lowest-energy state; a bubble of true vacuum could nucleate and expand at near light speed, rewriting physics.
status: Higgs and top-quark masses place the Standard Model near metastability (Degrassi et al. 2012); timescales vastly exceed the universe's age; depends on unknown physics.
proposal: Dome catastrophe: one rare spark converts the dome to new rules; the creature must detect early bubble signatures.

name: Degenerate and dark eras
origin_source: Adams and Laughlin 1997 (Rev. Mod. Phys. 69:337); 'The Five Ages of the Universe' 1999
core_idea: Timeline after the stars: degenerate era (white dwarfs, neutron stars), black-hole era, then a dark era of photons and leptons.
status: Mainstream extrapolation, with caveats (proton decay unconfirmed).
proposal: HEPTARCH LongGame: the late eras offer a template for scarcity-mode strategy.

category: Megastructures and limits (brief; see Post PDF)
name: Kardashev scale
core_idea: Rank civilizations by energy use: planetary, stellar, galactic. Humanity is about 0.73 on Sagan's interpolation.
status: Heuristic, not a theory. Detailed in the Post PDF (megastructure ladder).
proposal: Dome progress meter: track the creature's energy capture on a Kardashev-like scale.

category: Megastructures and limits (brief; see Post PDF)
name: Dyson sphere / swarm
core_idea: An advanced civilization surrounds its star with collectors, glowing in the infrared.
status: Engineering speculation; infrared searches (e.g. Project Hephaistos 2024 candidates) remain unconfirmed. See Post PDF.
proposal: Dome milestone: building an enclosure around the dome's energy source.

category: Megastructures and limits (brief; see Post PDF)
name: Matrioshka brain
origin_source: Bradbury, draft essay c.1997-1999 (date approximate, unverified)
core_idea: Nested shells around a star, each running computation on the waste heat of the inner shell.
status: Pure engineering speculation. See Post PDF ladder.
proposal: Dome motif: layered compute rings where each layer lives off the previous layer's waste.

name: Copenhagen interpretation
origin_source: Bohr 1927 (Como lecture); Heisenberg 1927-1930; label 'Copenhagen' from Heisenberg 1955
core_idea: Quantum states encode what can be predicted about measurement outcomes; measurement yields a definite classical result and the theory says nothing beyond that.
status: Still the textbook default, though 'Copenhagen' covers several incompatible views.
proposal: QWM: an instrumentalist stance: the latent is a predictor of observations, not a picture of hidden reality.

name: Many-worlds interpretation
origin_source: Everett 1957 (Rev. Mod. Phys. 29:454); named by DeWitt 1970
core_idea: The wavefunction never collapses; every quantum outcome happens, each in its own decohered branch.
status: Serious contender (Deutsch, Wallace, Carroll); open problems: the origin of Born-rule probabilities, ontological extravagance.
touchstones: Everything Everywhere All at Once; Dark Matter (Crouch)
proposal: Dome rule: forked replays; HEPTARCH can be run as branching copies, and the creature may notice divergent 'histories'.

name: Pilot-wave theory
core_idea: Particles always have positions, guided by a real wave; the theory is deterministic but explicitly nonlocal.
status: Empirically equivalent to standard QM for non-relativistic cases; relativistic extension is hard.
touchstones: Walking-droplet analog experiments (Couder 2005) as popular visual
proposal: Dome mechanic: hidden 'guide field' that steers objects; the creature sees only outcomes.

name: Objective collapse (GRW, Penrose OR)
origin_source: Ghirardi, Rimini, Weber 1986 (Phys. Rev. D 34:470); Diosi 1987; Penrose 1996 (Gen. Rel. Grav. 28:581)
core_idea: Wavefunctions collapse spontaneously and physically, more often for big objects, possibly triggered by gravity.
status: Testable and being tested; Gran Sasso radiation limits (Donadi et al. 2021, Nature Physics) ruled out the simplest Diosi-Penrose model.
proposal: Dome physics: big things are forced to be definite; small things can stay blurred.

name: Consistent histories
origin_source: Griffiths 1984 (J. Stat. Phys. 36:219); Omnes 1988; Gell-Mann and Hartle 1990
core_idea: Quantum theory assigns probabilities to sets of histories that do not interfere; no single history is privileged.
status: Respected but niche; critics cite many incompatible frameworks.
proposal: QWM: evaluate predicted rollouts only within sets that do not interfere.

name: QBism
origin_source: Caves, Fuchs, Schack 2002 (Phys. Rev. A 65); Fuchs 2010
core_idea: Quantum states are an agent's personal degrees of belief about their future experiences, not features of the world.
status: Live but minority interpretation; criticized as solipsism-adjacent.
proposal: QWM: the world model's latent is explicitly the agent's betting book; HEPTARCH's beliefs are its own, not the dome's.

name: Relational quantum mechanics
core_idea: Physical properties exist only relative to other systems; there is no observer-independent state of the world.
status: Serious philosophical interpretation; debated consistency claims.
proposal: Dome rule: facts are per-observer; two seats of HEPTARCH can hold different but consistent facts.

name: Transactional interpretation
origin_source: Cramer 1986 (Rev. Mod. Phys. 58:647); built on Wheeler-Feynman absorber theory 1945
core_idea: Quantum events are handshakes between waves going forward and backward in time.
status: Minority; retrocausal, compatible with standard predictions.
proposal: Dome puzzle: outcomes look 'pre-arranged' by future receivers.

name: Superdeterminism
origin_source: Bell 1985 interview (BBC 'Ghost in the Atom'); 't Hooft 2016 'The Cellular Automaton Interpretation'; Hossenfelder and Palmer 2020
core_idea: Bell-test 'loopholes' close if detector settings and particles are correlated from the start, so everything is predetermined.
status: Minority, widely criticized as conspiratorial; proponents propose specific tests.
proposal: Dome rule: the dome's seed fixes everything, including the creature's 'choices'; a test for whether it can detect this.

name: Schrodinger's cat
core_idea: A cat linked to a quantum trigger would be both alive and dead until observed, showing how odd it is to scale up superposition.
status: Intended as a criticism; now a symbol for the measurement problem. Lab 'cat states' of growing size are real.
proposal: Dome puzzle box: a sealed chamber whose content is undetermined until the creature opens it.

name: Wigner's friend
origin_source: Wigner 1961 ('Remarks on the mind-body question'); Frauchiger and Renner 2018 (Nat. Commun. 9:3711); Bong et al. 2020 (Nature Physics) 'local friendliness'
core_idea: A friend measures a system inside a lab while Wigner treats the whole lab as in superposition; whose facts are real?
status: Small-scale photonic versions (Proietti et al. 2019) show tensions among assumptions; no conscious 'friend' was involved.
proposal: Dome test: nested observers inside the dome disagree; the creature must reconcile reports from 'friend' sub-agents.

name: Quantum suicide and immortality
core_idea: Under many-worlds, a person facing a 50/50 quantum death trigger would always find themselves in a surviving branch.
status: Rejected as a survival mechanism: deaths are not clean binary quantum events and 'branch-indexed survival' misreads identity. Not an action guide.
proposal: Dome rule: survivor bias; only creatures that survive leave logs, so the creature must correct for survivorship.

name: Elitzur-Vaidman bomb tester
origin_source: Elitzur and Vaidman 1993 (Found. Phys. 23:987); Kwiat et al. 1995 demo
core_idea: Quantum interference can reveal a live bomb without it ever absorbing a photon.
status: Experimentally demonstrated (interaction-free measurement).
proposal: Dome puzzle: detect a trap without touching it, a model for Recon scouts.

name: Quantum Zeno effect
origin_source: Misra and Sudarshan 1977 (J. Math. Phys. 18:756); Itano et al. 1990 experiment
core_idea: Frequent measurement can freeze the evolution of a quantum system.
status: Established in experiments.
proposal: Dome mechanic: objects that change only when unobserved.

name: EPR paradox and Bell's theorem
origin_source: Einstein, Podolsky, Rosen 1935 (Phys. Rev. 47:777); Bell 1964 (Physics 1:195); Aspect 1982; loophole-free tests 2015 (Hensen et al., Nature 526)
core_idea: No local hidden-variable theory reproduces quantum correlations; nature violates Bell inequalities.
status: Established (Nobel 2022 to Aspect, Clauser, Zeilinger). It forbids local realism, not faster-than-light signalling.
proposal: Dome law: paired tokens whose correlations exceed any local strategy; the creature can discover a Bell inequality.

name: Delayed-choice experiments and quantum eraser
origin_source: Wheeler 1978; Scully and Druhl 1982 (Phys. Rev. A 25:2208); Kim et al. 2000 (PRL 84:1)
core_idea: Choosing later whether to learn which path a photon took appears to decide its earlier behaviour.
status: Experiments confirmed; mainstream reading: no retrocausation, only correlations visible after sorting data.
proposal: Dome puzzle: a record that seems to rewrite the past, until the creature learns the sorting trick.

name: Retrocausal quantum models
origin_source: Costa de Beauregard 1953; Price 1996 'Time's Arrow and Archimedes' Point'; Wharton and Argaman 2020 review
core_idea: Quantum correlations may arise because future measurement settings influence the past.
status: Minority but active research program.
proposal: Dome mechanic: future goals leave faint traces in present sensor data.

name: Wheeler-Feynman absorber theory
core_idea: Radiation is half retarded, half advanced; absorbers in the future complete every emission.
status: Historically influential; not standard. Ancestor of the transactional interpretation.
proposal: Dome rule: signals 'need a receiver'; an empty future blocks emission.

name: One-electron universe
origin_source: Wheeler, phone call to Feynman, spring 1940, as recounted in Feynman's Nobel lecture 1965
core_idea: All electrons are one electron zigzagging back and forth in time; positrons are its backward legs.
status: A playful idea. Feynman objected that there are not as many positrons as electrons; the backward-in-time view of positrons survived in Feynman diagrams.
proposal: Dome motif: a single agent replayed many times; each copy is the same creature at another time.

name: Holographic principle
origin_source: 't Hooft 1993 (gr-qc/9310026); Susskind 1995 (J. Math. Phys. 36:6377); Bekenstein 1973 entropy
core_idea: The information in a volume of space is bounded by and may be encoded on its boundary area.
status: Strongly supported in theory (black-hole entropy, AdS/CFT); not directly observed for our universe.
proposal: Dome law: the dome's full state is encoded on its shell; the creature can learn the interior from the boundary.

name: AdS/CFT correspondence
core_idea: A gravitational theory in anti-de Sitter space is exactly equivalent to a quantum field theory without gravity on its boundary.
status: Best-tested concrete holography; our universe is not AdS, so applicability is open.
proposal: QWM: two equivalent descriptions of one world, a template for latent/observation duality.

name: ER=EPR
core_idea: Entangled particles are connected by microscopic wormholes; entanglement and geometry are the same thing.
status: Serious conjecture; 'wormhole on a quantum chip' (Jafferis et al., Nature 2022) was a simulation of a toy model and its interpretation was disputed.
proposal: Dome law: entangling two objects literally shortens the path between them.

name: Spacetime from entanglement
origin_source: Van Raamsdonk 2010 (Gen. Rel. Grav. 42:2323); Ryu and Takayanagi 2006
core_idea: Space itself is stitched together by quantum entanglement; remove entanglement and space falls apart.
status: Active research (It from Qubit collaboration 2015-2023); no direct test yet.
proposal: QWM: latent geometry derived from correlation structure, distance as mutual information.

name: Black-hole firewall
core_idea: Preserving information may require a wall of high-energy quanta at the horizon, contradicting the 'no drama' prediction of GR.
status: Unresolved; 'island' and replica-wormhole results (2019-20) reshaped the debate.
proposal: Dome boundary: crossing the edge is lethal or harmless depending on which law is true; a test the creature can design.

name: Traversable wormholes
origin_source: Einstein and Rosen 1935 (Phys. Rev. 48:73); Morris and Thorne 1988 (Am. J. Phys. 56:395)
core_idea: Tunnels through spacetime connecting distant regions, kept open by exotic negative-energy matter.
status: Allowed by GR with exotic matter; no evidence; quantum inequalities strongly limit it.
proposal: Dome shortcut: costly portals that the creature can open only by spending 'negative' resources.

name: Tachyons
origin_source: Bilaniuk, Deshpande, Sudarshan 1962; Feinberg 1967 (Phys. Rev. 159:1089) named them
core_idea: Hypothetical particles that always travel faster than light.
status: Not observed; in modern field theory a 'tachyon' signals an instability, not a fast particle. OPERA's 2011 FTL neutrinos were a cable fault.
proposal: Dome red herring: a signal that looks faster than light but traces to a wiring error.

name: Negative mass
core_idea: Matter with negative mass would accelerate toward pushes and could enable runaway motion and warp drives.
status: No evidence; 'effective negative mass' in fluids (2017) is an analogy, not true negative mass.
proposal: Dome exotic: one resource with inverted inertia, enabling 'impossible' moves at a price.

name: Mach's principle
origin_source: Mach 1883 (The Science of Mechanics); named by Einstein 1918
core_idea: Inertia arises from the influence of all the mass in the universe.
status: Partly reflected in GR (frame-dragging, measured by Gravity Probe B 2011) but not fully implemented.
proposal: Dome law: an object's 'heaviness' depends on what else is in the dome.

name: Magnetic monopoles
origin_source: Dirac 1931 (Proc. R. Soc. A 133:60); 't Hooft and Polyakov 1974
core_idea: Isolated north or south magnetic charges; their existence would explain why electric charge is quantized.
status: Not found in nature (one 1982 Cabrera event never repeated); emergent monopoles seen in spin ice.
proposal: Dome treasure: one rare 'charge' that, once found, explains a regularity the creature noticed.

name: Zero-point energy and the Casimir effect
core_idea: Even empty space has quantum fluctuations with measurable effects such as the Casimir force.
status: Casimir force is established; free-energy 'zero-point machines' are not.
proposal: Dome law: vacuum pressure is real but cannot be mined for perpetual work.

name: Maxwell's demon
origin_source: Maxwell 1867 letter to Tait; Theory of Heat 1871; Szilard 1929; Landauer 1961; Bennett 1982
core_idea: A tiny being sorting fast and slow molecules would beat the second law; resolved because erasing its memory costs energy.
status: Resolved through information thermodynamics; Landauer's limit measured (Berut et al., Nature 2012).
proposal: Dome law: information is physical; forgetting costs energy. HEPTARCH's memory pruning has a price.

name: Landauer's principle
core_idea: Erasing one bit of information releases at least kT ln 2 of heat.
status: Established experimentally (2012 onward). Detailed in the Post PDF physical-limits section.
proposal: Dome accounting: every deletion heats the dome; reversible moves are cheaper.

name: Feynman's Brownian ratchet
core_idea: A tiny ratchet seems able to extract work from random molecular motion, but at equal temperatures it cannot.
status: Established resolution; molecular motors work because they are out of equilibrium.
proposal: Dome law: no free work from noise unless the creature finds a temperature difference.

name: Block universe (eternalism)
core_idea: Past, present and future all exist equally; 'now' is like 'here'.
status: Widely held among physicists because relativity has no universal present; contested by presentists.
proposal: Dome view: logs of the whole run exist at once; the creature's 'now' is an index into them.

name: Presentism
origin_source: Classic: Augustine, Confessions XI (c.400); modern Prior 1970
core_idea: Only present things exist; past and future are not real.
status: Philosophically live; difficult to reconcile with relativity's relativity of simultaneity.
proposal: Dome design: no stored past, only present state; memory must be built by the creature.

name: Growing block universe
core_idea: Past and present exist and the future does not yet; reality grows as time passes.
status: Live philosophical option; Ellis argues quantum events 'crystallize' the block.
proposal: Dome: an append-only world log, the natural form for a simulated arena.

name: Unreality of time (McTaggart)
core_idea: Time requires an A-series (past, present, future), which is contradictory, so time is unreal.
status: Argument rejected by most, but the A/B distinction it introduced structures the field.
proposal: QWM: separate tense (A) from ordering (B) in temporal latents.

name: Timeless physics (Platonia)
origin_source: Barbour 1999 'The End of Time'; Wheeler-DeWitt equation 1967
core_idea: Time does not exist fundamentally; there are only static configurations ('nows') and the illusion of flow comes from records within them.
status: Minority view; the 'problem of time' in quantum gravity is real.
proposal: Dome: shuffle frames; can the creature reconstruct order from internal records alone?

name: Arrow of time and the Past Hypothesis
origin_source: Eddington 1927 Gifford lectures (coined 'time's arrow'); Boltzmann 1877; Albert 2000 'Time and Chance' (named 'Past Hypothesis')
core_idea: Time's direction comes from entropy increase, which needs an extremely low-entropy beginning.
status: Mainstream explanation; why the start was low-entropy is an open glitch (see Part II).
proposal: Dome law: the creature can tell time's direction only by disorder growing.

name: Thermal time hypothesis
core_idea: Time is not fundamental; it emerges from the statistical state of a system.
status: Speculative but mathematically precise.
proposal: Dome clock: tick rate derived from the arena's statistical state, not a master clock.

name: Laplace's demon
origin_source: Laplace 1814 (Essai philosophique sur les probabilites); anticipated by Boscovich 1758
core_idea: An intellect knowing every particle's state and every law could compute the entire past and future.
status: Defeated in practice by chaos and quantum indeterminacy; Wolpert 2008 showed formal limits on any in-universe predictor.
proposal: Dome limit: no agent inside the dome can perfectly predict the dome including itself.

name: Aristotle's sea battle
core_idea: If 'there will be a sea battle tomorrow' is already true or false, the future seems fixed.
status: Classic logic problem; motivated three-valued logic (Lukasiewicz 1920).
proposal: Dome logic: statements about tomorrow get a third truth value until resolved.

name: Grandfather paradox
origin_source: Popular form in SF from 1920s-30s; Barjavel 1943 'Le Voyageur imprudent' often cited
core_idea: Travelling back and preventing your own birth seems contradictory.
status: Classic tool; motivates self-consistency and branching resolutions.
proposal: Dome rule: forbid or branch actions that delete the actor's own origin.

name: Bootstrap (ontological) paradox
core_idea: An object or idea exists without origin because it is passed around a time loop.
status: Logically consistent in some GR models; violates intuitions about creation of information.
proposal: Dome puzzle: an artefact whose design came from the creature's own future log.

name: Polchinski's billiard-ball paradox
origin_source: Polchinski, letter to Thorne, c.1990; Echeverria, Klinkhammer, Thorne 1991 (Phys. Rev. D 44:1077)
core_idea: A ball sent through a wormhole time machine could knock its earlier self off course.
status: Analysis found self-consistent solutions exist for every initial condition studied.
proposal: Dome physics test: simulate the billiard paradox in the dome and see which consistent loop the solver picks.

name: Tachyonic antitelephone
origin_source: Tolman 1917 (The Theory of the Relativity of Motion); Benford, Book, Newcomb 1970 (Phys. Rev. D 2:263)
core_idea: FTL signals would let you send a message into your own past, creating paradoxes.
status: Accepted logic; one reason FTL is considered impossible.
proposal: Dome law: any FTL channel the creature finds also implies a time channel; it must reason about that.

name: Novikov self-consistency principle
origin_source: Novikov, 1980s; Friedman, Morris, Novikov et al. 1990 (Phys. Rev. D 42:1915)
core_idea: The only histories that occur with time travel are self-consistent ones; paradoxes have zero probability.
status: Mainstream conjecture for classical CTCs.
touchstones: Twelve Monkeys; Harry Potter Prisoner of Azkaban
proposal: Dome rule: actions on loops are constrained to be consistent; the solver enforces it.

name: Deutsch's quantum time travel (D-CTCs)
origin_source: Deutsch 1991 (Phys. Rev. D 44:3197); Lloyd et al. 2011 P-CTCs
core_idea: Quantum mechanics allows consistent time travel if travellers enter a different branch; paradoxes resolve as mixed states.
status: Theoretical; implies huge computational power (Aaronson and Watrous 2009). See Post PDF CTC computing.
proposal: QWM: a fixed-point solver for loops; the dome could host a sandboxed loop puzzle.

name: Chronology protection conjecture
core_idea: The laws of physics prevent time machines from forming, e.g. vacuum fluctuations blow up as a time machine nears completion.
status: Unproven conjecture; widely suspected true.
proposal: Dome safeguard: any loop-building attempt triggers a growing instability.

name: Godel rotating universe
core_idea: An exact GR solution for a rotating universe contains closed timelike curves, so time travel is allowed in principle.
status: Mathematically valid; does not describe our non-rotating universe.
touchstones: Philosophy of time; Godel's 'time is ideal' argument
proposal: Dome variant: a rotating dome with loop-paths built into its geometry.

name: Tipler cylinder
core_idea: A massive, very fast-spinning infinitely long cylinder would allow loops in time.
status: Requires infinite length or exotic matter (Hawking 1992).
proposal: Dome toy: a spinning pillar whose orbit lands the creature earlier in the log.

name: Gott cosmic-string time machine
core_idea: Two cosmic strings passing at high speed create closed timelike curves.
status: Shown to need unphysical conditions (Deser, Jackiw, 't Hooft 1992).
proposal: Dome exotic: paired 'strings' passing each other make a brief loop window.

name: Alcubierre warp drive
core_idea: Contract space ahead and expand space behind a bubble to move faster than light without local FTL motion.
status: Needs negative energy; 2021 'positive-energy' proposals (Lentz; Bobrick and Martire) are debated.
proposal: Dome mobility: the creature can bend its arena's metric locally at an energy price.

name: Krasnikov tube
core_idea: A spacetime tube built on an outward trip allows a fast return trip.
status: Also needs exotic matter.
proposal: Dome road-building: the first trip is slow, the return fast.

name: Eternal recurrence
origin_source: Nietzsche 1882 'The Gay Science' sec. 341; earlier Stoics and Pythagoreans
core_idea: Everything that happens will happen again, infinitely, in the same order.
status: As cosmology, unsupported; as an ethical test ('would you will it again?') influential.
proposal: HEPTARCH test: does the creature choose differently when it believes the episode repeats forever?

name: Poincare recurrence
core_idea: A bounded isolated system will return arbitrarily close to its starting state after enough time.
status: Mathematical theorem; recurrence times for macroscopic systems are absurdly long.
proposal: Dome law: a finite dome will eventually repeat; the creature could estimate the period.

name: The hard problem of consciousness
origin_source: Chalmers 1995 (J. Consciousness Studies 2:200); Levine 1983 'explanatory gap' (Pac. Phil. Q. 64:354)
core_idea: Explaining brain functions does not obviously explain why there is subjective experience at all.
status: Widely acknowledged; illusionists deny it is a real problem. Open (see Part II).
proposal: Paper rule: the QWM template makes no claim about experience in any model; HEPTARCH is described functionally only.

name: What is it like to be a bat?
core_idea: Even complete knowledge of bat biology would not tell us what echolocation feels like to the bat.
status: Classic; central to debates on subjectivity.
proposal: QWM: alien sensor modalities (omni-harness) produce latents the designers cannot 'feel'; design must rely on behaviour.

name: Mary's room
core_idea: A scientist who knows all physical facts about colour but has only seen black and white seems to learn something new on seeing red.
status: Ongoing debate; responses include ability and acquaintance hypotheses.
proposal: Dome test: give the creature full data about a channel it has never sensed, then open the channel; measure behaviour change.

name: Philosophical zombies
core_idea: A being physically identical to a person but with no experience; if conceivable, physicalism is in trouble.
status: Contested: conceivability may not imply possibility.
proposal: Paper stance: behaviour cannot settle experience questions, which is exactly why the QWM paper avoids them.

name: Inverted spectrum
core_idea: Two people could see colours swapped while behaving identically.
status: Classic tool; debated whether coherent given colour-space asymmetries.
proposal: Dome: two seats map the same input to swapped internal codes; do they still coordinate?

name: The Chinese Room
core_idea: A person following rules to answer Chinese questions understands no Chinese, so symbol manipulation alone is not understanding.
status: Still debated (systems reply, robot reply). Here used only as a philosophy-of-language puzzle; no claim about any AI's experience.
proposal: HEPTARCH relevance: being tokenless and grounded in its dome is the 'robot reply' design choice; it says nothing about experience.

name: China brain
core_idea: If the whole population of China simulated a brain's functional organization by radio, would there be a mind?
status: Classic challenge to functionalism.
touchstones: The Three-Body Problem's human computer scene (Liu Cixin)
proposal: Dome motif: a swarm of simple agents jointly running one seat.

name: Leibniz's mill
core_idea: Enlarge a thinking machine to the size of a mill and walk inside; you see only parts pushing parts, never perception.
status: Ancestor of the hard problem.
proposal: Interpretability caution: inspecting HEPTARCH's parts explains function, not 'what it is like'.

name: Turing test
core_idea: If a machine's conversation is indistinguishable from a person's, we should credit it with thinking.
status: Historic benchmark; widely regarded as testing behaviour, not experience.
proposal: HEPTARCH is tokenless, so the test is irrelevant to it; dome behaviour tests replace it.

name: Panpsychism
origin_source: Ancient: Thales (c.600 BCE, 'all things are full of gods'); modern: Strawson 2006; Goff 2019 'Galileo's Error'
core_idea: Some rudimentary form of mind is a fundamental feature of all matter.
status: Minority but growing in philosophy; faces the 'combination problem'. Empirically untested.
proposal: Philosophy only: noted, not adopted; the dome has no 'mind-stuff' variable.

name: Cosmopsychism
origin_source: Shani 2015; Nagasawa and Wager 2016; roots in Advaita and Spinoza
core_idea: The cosmos as a whole is the fundamental conscious subject, and individual minds are aspects of it.
status: Speculative metaphysics.
proposal: Philosophy only.

name: Cartesian dualism
core_idea: Mind and body are distinct substances that interact.
status: Minority among philosophers; interaction problem.
proposal: Dome note: HEPTARCH has no separate 'soul' channel; all state is in-dome.

name: Neutral monism
origin_source: James 1904; Russell 1921 'The Analysis of Mind'; Eddington 1928
core_idea: Mind and matter are two ways of organizing one underlying neutral stuff.
status: Live option in philosophy of mind.
proposal: Philosophy only.

name: Illusionism about consciousness
core_idea: Phenomenal consciousness as usually conceived is an introspective illusion; explain the illusion instead.
status: Serious minority position.
proposal: Design note: functional self-models in HEPTARCH can be studied without any experience claim.

name: Integrated information theory (as a claim)
core_idea: Consciousness is identical to integrated causal structure, measured by phi.
status: Contested: in 2023 more than 100 researchers signed a letter calling it pseudoscience; adversarial tests vs global workspace (Nature 2025) were mixed. Philosophy only here; no claim about any AI.
proposal: Philosophy only; HEPTARCH metrics stay behavioural.

name: Global workspace theory
origin_source: Baars 1988 'A Cognitive Theory of Consciousness'; Dehaene and Naccache 2001
core_idea: Conscious content is information broadcast widely across a brain-wide workspace.
status: Leading scientific theory of human access consciousness; partly challenged by 2025 adversarial results.
proposal: Architecture analogy only: HEPTARCH's seat bus is a broadcast workspace in the engineering sense.

name: Orchestrated objective reduction
core_idea: Consciousness arises from quantum computations in neuron microtubules ended by gravity-induced collapse.
status: Fringe-to-contested; decoherence estimates (Tegmark 2000) argue against it; some 2024 anaesthesia-microtubule studies are cited by proponents.
proposal: Not used; HEPTARCH's 'quantum' parts are classical simulations.

name: Free-energy principle
core_idea: Living systems persist by minimizing surprise (variational free energy) about their sensory states.
status: Influential framework; critics call it unfalsifiable as stated.
proposal: QWM link: JEPA-style prediction error and active inference share the predictive-processing core.

name: Ship of Theseus
origin_source: Plutarch, Life of Theseus 23 (c.75 CE); Hobbes 1655 'De Corpore' (the rebuilt-ship twist)
core_idea: If every plank is replaced, is it the same ship? And if the old planks are reassembled, which is the original?
status: Classic identity puzzle; no consensus.
proposal: HEPTARCH: after every seat is retrained, is it the same creature? Define identity by lineage hash.

name: Teletransportation paradox
core_idea: A teleporter scans you, destroys you and builds a copy elsewhere; did you travel or die?
status: Central to identity debates.
proposal: Dome: copying HEPTARCH into a new dome raises the same question; log it as a fork with shared ancestry.

name: Parfit's fission and 'identity is not what matters'
core_idea: If you split into two equally good continuers, neither is you; what matters is psychological continuity, not identity.
status: Influential; contested.
proposal: HEPTARCH fork policy: treat continuity as degree, not yes or no.

name: Swampman
origin_source: Davidson 1987 ('Knowing One's Own Mind', Proc. APA 60:441)
core_idea: Lightning creates a molecule-for-molecule copy of Davidson; does the copy's speech mean anything without history?
status: Debate on content externalism.
proposal: Dome: a creature spawned with copied weights but no lived history; does its memory 'refer'?

name: Prince and cobbler (body swap)
core_idea: If a prince's consciousness entered a cobbler's body, the person would go with the memories.
status: Origin of psychological-continuity theories.
proposal: Dome: swap two seats' memories between bodies and test which identity the others track.

name: Bundle theory of the self
origin_source: Hume 1739 'Treatise' I.iv.6; parallel to Buddhist anatta
core_idea: The self is nothing but a bundle of perceptions in flux.
status: Live view; resonates with Buddhist no-self.
proposal: HEPTARCH framing: seven seats as a bundle; 'self' as a coordination label.

name: Extended mind
core_idea: Notebooks and tools can literally be part of the mind if they play the right role.
status: Influential; debated.
proposal: HEPTARCH: dome-written markers count as part of its memory system.

name: Mind uploading and gradual replacement
origin_source: Moravec 1988 'Mind Children'; Chalmers 1996 'fading qualia'; Sandberg and Bostrom 2008 roadmap
core_idea: Replace neurons one by one with chips, or scan and emulate a brain, and the person may continue in a new substrate.
status: Far beyond current technology; identity questions unresolved. See Post PDF.
proposal: Not a HEPTARCH goal; noted for the Post PDF only.

name: Allegory of the cave
core_idea: Prisoners see only shadows on a wall and take them for reality; the philosopher escapes to see the sun.
status: Foundational allegory for appearance versus reality.
proposal: Dome arc: the creature sees projections on the dome shell; inferring the projector is the escape quest.

name: Zhuangzi's butterfly dream
core_idea: Zhuangzi dreamt he was a butterfly; on waking he could not tell if he was a man who dreamt of a butterfly or a butterfly dreaming it was a man.
status: Classic Daoist meditation on transformation and perspective.
touchstones: Inception; Ghost in the Shell references
proposal: Dome: HEPTARCH 'dream' replays (offline training) labelled indistinguishably from live play, then a test of which it is in.

name: Dream argument
core_idea: There are no certain marks to distinguish waking from dreaming.
status: Classic skeptical argument.
proposal: QWM: world models need a 'reality check' signal separating imagined from sensed rollouts.

name: Descartes' evil demon
origin_source: Descartes 1641 'Meditations' I; cogito in Discourse on Method 1637
core_idea: An all-powerful deceiver might be feeding me every experience; only 'I think, I am' survives.
status: Foundational skeptical tool.
proposal: HEPTARCH: if the host can deceive the creature, what can it still be sure of? Its own processing.

name: Brain in a vat
origin_source: Harman 1973 'Thought'; Putnam 1981 'Reason, Truth and History' ch. 1 (semantic externalist reply)
core_idea: A disembodied brain stimulated by a computer would have the same experiences as you.
status: Putnam argued 'I am a brain in a vat' is self-refuting if meaning depends on causal contact. Tool, not a claim.
proposal: Dome: HEPTARCH literally is in a 'vat'; by Putnam's logic its word for 'tree' refers to dome-trees.

name: Solipsism
origin_source: Gorgias c.400 BCE (attributed, via Sextus Empiricus); modern discussions from Descartes onward
core_idea: Only my mind is sure to exist; the world and other minds may be my projections.
status: Irrefutable and unpopular.
proposal: Dome: a single-agent dome where other agents are host-scripted; can the creature detect scripted vs learning agents?

name: Last Thursdayism, Omphalos and the five-minute hypothesis
origin_source: Gosse 1857 'Omphalos'; Russell 1921 'The Analysis of Mind' (five minutes ago); 'Last Thursdayism' is a later internet-era parody (origin unclear)
core_idea: The world might have been created recently, complete with fossils, starlight and memories.
status: Unfalsifiable; used to illustrate the limits of evidence about the past.
proposal: HEPTARCH: every dome boot is 'last Thursday'; memories are seeded. Honest design: give the creature a boot-stamp it can find.

name: Agrippa's / Munchhausen trilemma
origin_source: Agrippa via Sextus Empiricus, Outlines of Pyrrhonism I.164-177 (c.200 CE); Albert 1968 (Munchhausen)
core_idea: Any justification ends in infinite regress, circularity or a dogmatic stopping point.
status: Standard epistemology problem.
proposal: QWM: every model's priors are a dogmatic stop; document them.

name: Problem of induction
origin_source: Hume 1739 Treatise; 1748 Enquiry IV; Russell's chicken 1912
core_idea: No non-circular argument shows the future will resemble the past.
status: Unsolved in principle; Bayesian and Solomonoff approaches manage it in practice.
proposal: HEPTARCH: dome laws may change; build drift detection rather than assuming stationarity.

name: Goodman's grue
core_idea: 'Grue' (green until 2030, then blue) fits all evidence as well as 'green'; which predicates are projectable?
status: Unresolved; key to inductive bias.
proposal: Dome test: a property that flips at a hidden date; does the creature's bias choose 'green' or 'grue'?

name: Hempel's raven paradox
core_idea: A green apple confirms 'all non-black things are non-ravens', and so 'all ravens are black'.
status: Bayesian resolution: confirmation is tiny.
proposal: QWM: evidence weighting by informativeness.

name: Gettier problem
core_idea: Justified true belief can be true by luck, so it is not knowledge.
status: Classic; no agreed definition of knowledge since.
proposal: HEPTARCH: credit seats for being right for the right reasons, not luck.

name: Duhem-Quine thesis
core_idea: No hypothesis is tested alone; a failed prediction can always be blamed on an auxiliary assumption.
status: Accepted in philosophy of science.
proposal: ToE method: every glitch can be absorbed by tweaking auxiliaries; the weighing in Part III penalises tweaks.

name: Molyneux's problem
origin_source: Molyneux letter to Locke 1688; Locke Essay 2nd ed. 1694
core_idea: Would a person born blind, given sight, recognise a cube by sight alone?
status: Partly tested: Held et al. 2011 (Nature Neurosci.) found no immediate transfer in newly sighted patients.
proposal: Omni-harness test: does a newly added sensor map onto existing latents immediately?

name: Doomsday argument
origin_source: Carter 1983 (lecture); Leslie 1989/1996 'The End of the World'; Gott 1993 (Nature 363:315); Nielsen 1989
core_idea: If you are a random human in birth order, humanity is unlikely to last vastly longer than it has so far.
status: Contested; depends on the self-sampling assumption.
proposal: HEPTARCH LongGame: reason about its own 'birth rank' among dome generations.

name: Sleeping Beauty problem
core_idea: Woken once if heads, twice (with memory wiped) if tails: on waking, what is your credence in heads, 1/2 or 1/3?
status: Unresolved; 'thirders' and 'halfers' persist.
proposal: Dome: memory-wiped re-runs make this a live engineering question for HEPTARCH's self-location.

name: Self-sampling vs self-indication assumptions
core_idea: Rules for reasoning as if you were randomly chosen among observers; each gives paradoxical results (doomsday vs presumptuous philosopher).
status: Open.
proposal: QWM: explicit observer-weighting rule for branching world models.

name: Zeno's paradoxes
aliases: Achilles and the tortoise, the arrow, dichotomy
origin_source: Zeno of Elea c.450 BCE, via Aristotle Physics VI
core_idea: Motion seems impossible: to cross a distance you must first cross half, then half again, forever.
status: Mathematically resolved by convergent series and limits; some argue the physics of continuum remains open.
proposal: Dome law: discrete ticks dissolve Zeno; the creature can test whether its space is continuous.

name: Hilbert's Grand Hotel
origin_source: Hilbert lecture 1924; popularized by Gamow 1947 'One Two Three... Infinity'
core_idea: A full hotel with infinitely many rooms can still take infinitely many new guests.
status: Correct mathematics about infinite sets; physically infinite actual sets are debated.
proposal: Dome puzzle: an infinite-capacity 'hotel' room that teaches the creature countable infinity.

name: Cantor's diagonal argument and uncountability
core_idea: There are more real numbers than whole numbers; infinities come in sizes.
status: Theorem.
proposal: QWM: a world model cannot enumerate all possible worlds; it must sample.

name: Independence of the continuum hypothesis
core_idea: Whether there is an infinity between the integers and the reals cannot be decided from standard axioms.
status: Theorem (independence). Whether CH has a 'true' answer is debated.
proposal: Dome lesson: some questions have no answer inside the given rules.

name: Banach-Tarski paradox
core_idea: A solid ball can be cut into finitely many pieces and reassembled into two balls of the same size.
status: Theorem using the axiom of choice; pieces are non-measurable, so not physical.
proposal: Dome law: matter is measurable; such 'duplication' is impossible, a contrast lesson about math vs physics.

name: Thomson's lamp
core_idea: A lamp toggled infinitely often in two minutes: is it on or off at the end?
status: Shows supertasks may be ill-defined.
proposal: Dome: finite tick rate bans supertasks.

name: Gabriel's horn
core_idea: A horn with finite volume but infinite surface area: you could fill it with paint but not paint it.
status: Theorem; paradox dissolves on inspection.
proposal: Dome toy geometry.

name: Liar paradox
origin_source: Eubulides of Miletus c.350 BCE; Epimenides version (c.600 BCE attributed)
core_idea: 'This sentence is false' is true if false and false if true.
status: Responses: truth hierarchies (Tarski), paraconsistent logic (Priest).
proposal: Dome: self-referential signs that the creature must learn to quarantine.

name: Russell's paradox
core_idea: The set of all sets that do not contain themselves both does and does not contain itself.
status: Resolved by axiomatic set theory (ZF).
proposal: Paper: type discipline in the QWM's symbolic layer.

name: Sorites paradox
core_idea: Removing one grain never turns a heap into a non-heap, yet eventually no heap remains.
status: Vagueness unresolved (supervaluation, epistemicism, fuzzy logic).
proposal: HEPTARCH: categories in the dome are graded; seats use soft thresholds.

name: Unexpected hanging paradox
core_idea: A prisoner reasons he cannot be hanged by surprise on any day, and is then surprised.
status: Debated: self-reference in knowledge.
proposal: Dome event scheduler: surprise strikes that stay surprising despite reasoning.

name: Curry, Berry and Yablo paradoxes
core_idea: Self-reference variants: 'the smallest number not definable in under sixty letters'; 'if this is true, then pigs fly'; an infinite non-circular liar chain.
status: Logical tools; Berry underlies Chaitin's incompleteness.
proposal: Paper: definitional limits on any self-describing world model.

name: Godel's incompleteness theorems
core_idea: Any consistent formal system rich enough for arithmetic has true statements it cannot prove, and cannot prove its own consistency.
status: Theorems. Extensions to minds (Lucas 1961; Penrose 1989) are contested.
proposal: Dome lesson: the creature's rulebook cannot certify itself; a seat must look outside.

name: Tarski's undefinability of truth
core_idea: Arithmetical truth cannot be defined within arithmetic itself.
status: Theorem.
proposal: Paper: the model's 'truth' predicate must live one level up.

name: Skolem's paradox
core_idea: Set theory proves uncountable sets exist, yet has a countable model.
status: Resolved: 'uncountable' is relative to the model.
proposal: Dome: 'infinite' inside the dome can be finite from the host's view.

name: Halting problem
core_idea: No algorithm can decide for every program whether it eventually halts.
status: Theorem; ties to Rice's theorem and undecidable physics (Cubitt et al. 2015 spectral gap).
proposal: Dome law: some futures are uncomputable even for the host; forecasting has a hard limit.

name: Physical Church-Turing thesis
origin_source: Church 1936; Turing 1936; physical version Deutsch 1985 (Proc. R. Soc. A 400:97)
core_idea: Every physically realizable process can be simulated by a universal (quantum) computer.
status: Widely accepted working hypothesis; hypercomputation proposals challenge it (see Post PDF).
proposal: Core ToE assumption for any simulation or ruliad view.

name: Busy beaver
origin_source: Rado 1962 (Bell Syst. Tech. J. 41:877); BB(5) = 47,176,870 proved 2024 (bbchallenge)
core_idea: The maximum steps a halting n-state Turing machine can take grows faster than any computable function.
status: Established; BB(5) proved in 2024 with Coq; BB(6) values relate to Collatz-like open problems.
proposal: Dome easter egg: a counter whose value the creature can never compute beyond a small n.

name: Chaitin's Omega
core_idea: A definable real number whose digits are maximally random and mostly unknowable.
status: Theorem.
proposal: Dome oracle: a sealed number whose first few digits are a prize.

name: Solomonoff induction and Kolmogorov complexity
core_idea: The ideal predictor weighs every computable hypothesis by its simplicity; it is uncomputable but defines optimal induction.
status: Theoretical gold standard; approximations underlie compression-based learning.
proposal: QWM: parsimony scoring in Part III is a crude Kolmogorov proxy.

name: Mathematical Universe Hypothesis
core_idea: External physical reality is a mathematical structure; all structures exist.
status: Contested metaphysics; criticized on measure and Godel grounds.
proposal: ToE-B ingredient: dome physics as one structure among many the host could run.

name: The ruliad
core_idea: The entangled limit of running all possible computations; physics is how observers like us sample it.
status: Not accepted by mainstream physics; criticized for lack of quantitative predictions.
proposal: ToE-B core: the dome as a computationally bounded observer's slice of rule-space.

name: Digital physics and cellular-automaton universe
core_idea: The universe is a discrete computation, like a cellular automaton.
status: Speculative; must reproduce Lorentz invariance and Bell violations.
proposal: Dome reality: HEPTARCH's dome is literally digital physics, the cleanest place to study it.

name: Conway's Game of Life as a universe
core_idea: Four simple rules on a grid produce gliders, self-replicators and universal computers.
status: Established mathematics; often used as a model of emergent physics.
proposal: Dome design: rules simple enough that the creature could rediscover them.

name: Simulation argument
core_idea: One of three is likely true: civilizations die before running ancestor simulations, choose not to run them, or we are almost certainly simulated.
status: Serious philosophical argument; a trilemma, not a proof. Critiques target its typicality assumptions. Full treatment in the Post PDF.
touchstones: The Matrix; The Thirteenth Floor; Black Mirror
proposal: HEPTARCH's dome IS a simulation; the design question is what in-world clues let it infer that.

name: Ancestor simulations
core_idea: Future civilizations could run detailed simulations of their ancestors. Cross-ref Post PDF.
status: Speculative; ethics strongly against.
proposal: Bright line: QWM does not simulate people.

name: Nested simulations
core_idea: Simulated civilizations could run simulations of their own, stacking levels with less compute at each level.
status: Speculation; compute limits pinch lower levels.
proposal: Dome inside dome: HEPTARCH could build a mini-dome; resources shrink at each level.

name: Simulation realism (Chalmers)
core_idea: If we are simulated, our tables and chairs are still real, just made of bits; a simulation is not an illusion.
status: Serious philosophical position.
proposal: Dome ethic: the creature's world is real for it; host design should respect that consistency.

name: Dust theory
core_idea: Any set of states, scattered anywhere and in any order, that can be read as a coherent mind experiences itself as continuous.
status: Fiction-born philosophy; related to Boltzmann-brain reasoning.
proposal: Dome experiment: shuffle the creature's state snapshots; does its behaviour stay consistent? (No experience claim.)

name: Lattice test of a simulated universe
origin_source: Beane, Davoudi, Savage 2014 (Eur. Phys. J. A 50:148), arXiv 2012
core_idea: If spacetime were a lattice simulation, the highest-energy cosmic rays would show directional anisotropy aligned with the lattice.
status: Testable in principle; no such signal found.
proposal: Dome probe: the creature looks for grid-aligned anisotropy at its highest energies.

name: Hacking or escaping the simulation
origin_source: Yampolskiy 2023 'How to Hack the Simulation?' (Philosophy and Cosmology, unverified pages)
core_idea: If we are simulated, glitches, exploits or communication with simulators might be possible.
status: Speculative; no accepted method.
proposal: HEPTARCH: the dome's 'bend the rules' feature: sanctioned exploits are logged, not hidden; the host stays read-only.

name: Computational limits on simulated universes
origin_source: Ringel and Kovrizhin 2017 (Science Advances 3:e1701758): sign problem in quantum Monte Carlo
core_idea: Some quantum effects appear to need exponentially growing classical resources, posing a cost to classical simulators.
status: Real result about classical algorithms; popular coverage overstated it as 'disproving' simulation.
proposal: Dome budget: quantum-like effects in the dome are expensive; that cost is itself a clue.

name: Berkeley's subjective idealism
core_idea: To be is to be perceived; objects exist as ideas in minds, kept continuous by God's perception.
status: Minority view; influential.
touchstones: The famous limerick on the tree in the quad
proposal: Dome efficiency: unobserved regions are not rendered, a game-engine analogy.

name: Kant's noumenon
core_idea: We know things only as they appear through our forms of intuition (space, time); things-in-themselves are unknowable.
status: Central to modern philosophy.
proposal: Dome: HEPTARCH knows the arena only through sensors; host code is its noumenon.

name: Spinoza's substance monism
core_idea: There is one substance, God or Nature, with infinite attributes; mind and matter are two of them.
status: Major metaphysics; inspired Einstein's 'Spinoza's God'.
proposal: ToE layering: one substrate, many descriptions.

name: Leibniz's monads and pre-established harmony
core_idea: Reality consists of windowless simple substances whose states are synchronized by God from the start.
status: Historic metaphysics; occasionally linked to relational physics.
proposal: HEPTARCH seats as 'windowless' modules synchronized by a shared clock.

name: Plato's theory of Forms
core_idea: Perfect abstract Forms are more real than their imperfect physical copies.
status: Mathematical Platonism remains a live view among mathematicians.
proposal: QWM: latent prototypes as 'forms' of observed objects.

name: Ontic structural realism
origin_source: Ladyman 1998 (Stud. Hist. Phil. Sci. 29:409); Worrall 1989 epistemic version
core_idea: Relations and structure are all there is; there are no objects underneath.
status: Serious in philosophy of physics.
proposal: ToE-A ingredient: reality as relational structure.

name: Maya (Advaita Vedanta)
origin_source: Shankara c.8th century CE; roots in the Upanishads
core_idea: The world of multiplicity is an appearance projected over the one reality, Brahman.
status: Living religious-philosophical tradition; not an empirical claim.
proposal: Dome narrative: the many objects of the dome as one underlying state vector rendered many ways.

name: Indra's net
origin_source: Avatamsaka Sutra; Huayan school, Fazang c.700 CE
core_idea: An infinite net with a jewel at each knot; each jewel reflects all the others.
status: Buddhist metaphor for interdependence; often compared to holography.
proposal: QWM: every latent node encodes a compressed view of the whole, holographic memory design.

name: Dependent origination
origin_source: Early Buddhist suttas (c.5th century BCE); Nagarjuna c.150 CE
core_idea: Nothing exists independently; everything arises in dependence on conditions.
status: Central Buddhist doctrine.
proposal: Dome causal graph: no object has intrinsic properties outside its relations.

name: Participatory anthropic universe
core_idea: Observers participate in bringing the universe into being; the universe is a self-excited circuit.
status: Speculative; inspired QBism and relational views.
proposal: Dome: the creature's measurements finalise undetermined dome regions.

name: It from bit
origin_source: Wheeler 1989 ('Information, physics, quantum: the search for links')
core_idea: Every physical thing derives its existence from yes-or-no answers, i.e. information.
status: Influential slogan; modern descendant is 'it from qubit'.
proposal: ToE-A core slogan.

name: Biocentrism
origin_source: Lanza 2007 (The American Scholar essay 'A New Theory of the Universe'); book with Berman 2009
core_idea: Life and consciousness create the universe rather than the reverse.
status: Rejected by mainstream physics; evidence shows a universe long before life.
proposal: Philosophy only.

name: Interface theory of perception
origin_source: Hoffman 2019 'The Case Against Reality'; Hoffman, Singh, Prakash 2015
core_idea: Evolution shapes perceptions to be useful icons, not true pictures; spacetime is a desktop interface.
status: Contested; simulations show fitness-tuned perception can beat truth-tuned perception in toy games.
proposal: HEPTARCH: train perception for payoff and check how far its icons drift from dome ground truth.

name: Modal realism
core_idea: All possible worlds exist as concretely as ours; 'actual' just means 'this one'.
status: Minority metaphysics ('incredulous stare').
proposal: QWM: counterfactual rollouts as 'possible worlds' with explicit weights.

name: Why is there something rather than nothing?
origin_source: Leibniz 1714 'Principles of Nature and Grace' sec. 7; Heidegger 1935
core_idea: The deepest question: why does anything exist at all?
status: Open; see Part II G10.
proposal: Dome: the creature cannot answer it about its dome without access to the host.

name: Primordial soup
core_idea: Life arose from organic molecules formed in an early ocean by energy input.
status: Partly supported (amino acids form readily); full pathway unknown.
proposal: Dome genesis: seed a primordial 'soup' of rule-fragments and watch for self-replication.

name: RNA world
origin_source: Woese 1967; Crick 1968; Orgel 1968; named by Gilbert 1986 (Nature 319:618)
core_idea: Early life used RNA for both genes and catalysis before DNA and proteins.
status: Leading hypothesis; ribozymes are real, but a self-replicating RNA from scratch is not yet shown.
proposal: Dome analog: one molecule type doubling as code and machine.

name: Hydrothermal-vent / metabolism-first origin
origin_source: Wachtershauser 1988; Russell and Martin 2003-2004; Lane 2015 'The Vital Question'
core_idea: Life began in alkaline vents where natural proton gradients powered metabolism before genes.
status: Serious hypothesis; competing with surface and wet-dry cycle scenarios.
proposal: Dome: energy gradients as the cradle of the first dome replicators.

name: Panspermia
origin_source: Anaxagoras (c.450 BCE, idea of seeds); Arrhenius 1903/1908; Hoyle and Wickramasinghe 1970s
core_idea: Life or its precursors travel between planets or stars, e.g. inside meteorites.
status: Lithopanspermia between Mars and Earth is physically possible; evidence of transfer is lacking.
proposal: Dome: life fragments migrate between neighbouring domes.

name: Directed panspermia
core_idea: An alien civilization deliberately seeded Earth with microbes.
status: Speculative; untested.
proposal: Dome origin myth the creature might infer: 'we were seeded'.

name: Shadow biosphere
origin_source: Cleland and Copley 2005 (Int. J. Astrobiol. 4:165); Davies et al. 2009
core_idea: A second, unrecognized form of life with different biochemistry could exist on Earth right now.
status: Speculative; no evidence; testable in principle.
proposal: Dome: hidden second ecology the creature's sensors are not tuned to.

name: Non-carbon life (silicon, ammonia, plasma)
origin_source: Weinbaum 1934 'A Martian Odyssey'; Sagan and Salpeter 1976 (Jovian floaters); Tsytovich et al. 2007 plasma crystals
core_idea: Life might be built on silicon, use ammonia as solvent, or even exist as self-organizing plasma.
status: Speculative; silicon chemistry is less versatile; Titan studies inform solvents.
touchstones: Star Trek 'Devil in the Dark' Horta
proposal: Dome biology: alternative 'chemistries' as rule-variants.

name: Gaia hypothesis
core_idea: Earth's life and environment form a self-regulating system that keeps conditions habitable.
status: Weak forms widely accepted (feedbacks exist); strong teleological forms rejected.
proposal: Dome: does the ecosystem of seats self-regulate the arena's 'climate'?

name: Medea hypothesis
core_idea: Life tends to be self-destructive, driving mass extinctions; the opposite of Gaia.
status: Contested.
proposal: Dome risk: an over-successful seat can collapse the arena; test both Gaia and Medea dynamics.

name: Dissipative adaptation
core_idea: Driven matter tends to organize into structures that absorb and dissipate energy well, a physical push toward life-like behaviour.
status: Interesting but contested and unproven for origin of life.
proposal: Dome law: driven arenas spontaneously organize; reward shaping from thermodynamics.

name: Assembly theory
origin_source: Cronin and Walker; Sharma et al. 2023 (Nature 622:321)
core_idea: Objects with high 'assembly index' that appear in many copies require selection, a measurable signature of life.
status: Controversial; critics say it reinvents complexity measures.
proposal: Dome detector: compute assembly index of dome objects to detect creature-made artefacts.

name: Von Neumann universal constructor
origin_source: von Neumann lectures 1948-49; published posthumously 1966 (Burks, ed.)
core_idea: A machine with a description tape can build any machine including a copy of itself, separating code from construction years before DNA's role was known.
status: Established theory of self-replication.
proposal: Dome: HEPTARCH spawning children uses an explicit constructor/tape split.

name: Artificial life: 'life as it could be'
origin_source: Langton 1987 (first ALife workshop, Los Alamos); Ray 1991 Tierra
core_idea: Life is a property of organization, not of carbon; it can be studied in software.
status: Weak ALife established; strong claim (software literally alive) debated. No consciousness claim implied.
proposal: HEPTARCH's home field; frame as 'life-like behaviour' without experience claims.

name: Edge of chaos
core_idea: Complex computation and life emerge near the boundary between order and chaos.
status: Influential but debated (Mitchell, Hraber, Crutchfield 1993 critique).
proposal: Dome tuning: set dome parameters near criticality to maximize interesting dynamics.

name: Fermi paradox
origin_source: Fermi, Los Alamos lunch 1950 (Jones 1985 LANL report); Hart 1975 (QJRAS 16:128) 'Fact A'; Tsiolkovsky 1933 earlier
core_idea: If intelligent life is common and old, why see no sign of it?
status: Recognized puzzle; dozens of proposed solutions.
proposal: Dome: the creature finds no other civilizations in its dome; which hypothesis does it adopt?

name: Drake equation
core_idea: Estimate communicating civilizations as a product of factors from star formation to civilization lifetime.
status: Heuristic; many terms unknown (Sandberg, Drexler, Ord 2018 'Dissolving the Fermi paradox').
proposal: Dome census: estimate how many other creatures should exist given dome rates.

name: Great Filter
origin_source: Hanson 1996 essay 'The Great Filter: Are We Almost Past It?' (web version dated 1998)
core_idea: Some step from dead matter to galaxy-spanning life is extremely improbable; it may lie ahead of us.
status: Serious framework; location of filter unknown.
proposal: HEPTARCH LongGame: identify the creature's own 'filters' and harden against them.

name: Rare Earth hypothesis
core_idea: Complex life needs an unusual combination of planetary and astronomical conditions.
status: Serious; contested by exoplanet abundance but not refuted.
proposal: Dome: many settings allow microbes, few allow complex creatures.

name: Grabby aliens
core_idea: Expanding civilizations will soon fill the universe; we are early because later observers get pre-empted.
status: Serious model with a predicted timeline; untested.
proposal: Dome: expansionist seats claim territory; early players have an advantage.

name: We are first (firstborn)
origin_source: Discussed by Hart 1975; Loeb, Batista, Sloan 2016 on cosmic earliness
core_idea: We see no one because we are among the first technological species.
status: Possible; consistent with the 'grabby' timing argument.
proposal: Dome: the creature is the first of its lineage; there is nobody to copy.

name: Zoo hypothesis
core_idea: Aliens know of us and deliberately avoid contact, as in a nature reserve.
status: Untestable; requires near-universal agreement among civilizations.
proposal: Dome: the host watches without interfering; can the creature detect observation?

name: Planetarium hypothesis
core_idea: Our view of the cosmos is a simulation built to hide a populated galaxy.
status: Speculative; would need enormous fidelity.
proposal: Dome sky as a painted ceiling; the creature tests parallax.

name: Dark Forest hypothesis
origin_source: Liu Cixin 2008 'The Dark Forest' (Chinese; English 2015); precursors: Saberhagen's Berserkers 1963, Brin 1983 (QJRAS 24:283) 'deadly probes'
core_idea: Civilizations hide because revealing yourself invites a pre-emptive strike from fearful others.
status: Fiction-born; game theorists question its assumptions (cooperation, detectability).
proposal: HEPTARCH: Raider cold-strike and Recon logic map directly onto dark-forest game theory.

name: Berserker / deadly probe hypothesis
core_idea: Self-replicating killer machines eliminate emerging civilizations.
status: Speculative.
proposal: Dome hazard: autonomous hunters triggered by detectable activity.

name: Aestivation hypothesis
core_idea: Advanced civilizations sleep until the universe cools, when computation is cheaper.
status: Speculative; Bennett, Hanson, Riedel 2019 rebutted the thermodynamics.
proposal: HEPTARCH LongGame: dormancy as strategy when the dome's 'temperature' will drop.

name: Transcension hypothesis
core_idea: Advanced civilizations migrate inward into dense inner space (black-hole-like computing) rather than outward.
status: Speculative.
proposal: Dome: the creature's optimum might be to compress, not expand.

name: Percolation theory of colonization
core_idea: Colonization spreads like percolation and leaves large empty voids, so we may be in one.
status: Speculative model.
proposal: Dome map: territory spreads in clusters, leaving gaps.

name: Silurian hypothesis
core_idea: Would we detect an industrial civilization that existed on Earth millions of years ago? Its geological traces would be subtle.
status: A framing question, not a claim; the authors doubt such a civilization existed.
proposal: Dome archaeology: prior HEPTARCH generations leave faint isotopic-like traces.

name: Simulation as Fermi answer
origin_source: Discussed in Bostrom 2003 context; Webb 2015 'If the Universe Is Teeming with Aliens'
core_idea: We see no aliens because the simulation only renders us.
status: Speculative.
proposal: Dome: host chooses not to render other civilizations; can the creature tell?

name: Von Neumann probes
origin_source: Self-replication theory: von Neumann 1948-66; probes: Bracewell 1960 (Nature 186:670) messenger probes; Freitas 1980 (JBIS 33:251) REPRO; Tipler 1980 (QJRAS 21:267)
core_idea: Self-copying probes could explore the galaxy in a few million years.
status: Engineering speculation; their absence is part of the Fermi argument. Von Neumann did not propose space probes himself.
proposal: Dome: child-spawning scouts mapping the arena.

name: Bracewell probe
core_idea: An autonomous alien probe may wait in our solar system to make contact.
status: Speculative; occasionally invoked for long-delayed echoes and 'Oumuamua.
proposal: Dome: a dormant host-placed beacon that wakes when the creature reaches a capability threshold.

name: METI / active SETI debate
origin_source: Arecibo message 1974; Zaitsev 2000s; critics Brin, Hawking 2010
core_idea: Should we broadcast to the stars? Proponents see little risk; critics fear dark-forest-style dangers.
status: Real policy debate.
proposal: HEPTARCH policy: when to reveal presence in the dome.

name: Newcomb's problem
origin_source: Newcomb (physicist) c.1960; Nozick 1969 ('Newcomb's Problem and Two Principles of Choice')
core_idea: A near-perfect predictor fills a box based on whether it predicts you take one box or both; one-box or two-box?
status: Unresolved; splits causal vs evidential decision theory.
proposal: Dome: host predictor offers boxes; tests HEPTARCH's decision theory.

name: Parfit's hitchhiker
core_idea: A driver who reads minds will save you only if you will truly pay later; must you be the kind of agent who pays?
status: Decision-theory puzzle.
proposal: HEPTARCH LongGame: reputation and precommitment.

name: Pascal's wager (and many-gods objection)
core_idea: Bet that God exists: infinite gain if right, finite loss if wrong.
status: Rejected by most philosophers (many-gods objection, infinity problems).
proposal: Decision hygiene: cap infinite payoffs in HEPTARCH utilities.

name: Pascal's mugging
core_idea: A stranger promises astronomically large rewards; tiny probabilities times huge payoffs dominate naive expected value.
status: Recognized decision-theory problem.
proposal: Dome safety: bounded utility and leverage penalties for huge-claim offers.

name: St Petersburg paradox
origin_source: N. Bernoulli 1713; D. Bernoulli 1738 (Comment. Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 5:175)
core_idea: A game with infinite expected value that no one would pay much to play.
status: Resolved in practice by diminishing utility and finite banks.
proposal: HEPTARCH: concave utility to avoid ruin bets.

name: Roko's basilisk
core_idea: A future superintelligence might punish those who knew of it and did not help create it.
status: Widely rejected: depends on contested acausal decision theory; Yudkowsky deleted the thread. A cautionary meme.
proposal: Anti-pattern: HEPTARCH must never use threats against past agents; documented as forbidden design.

name: Prisoner's dilemma
origin_source: Flood and Dresher, RAND 1950; named by Tucker 1950; Axelrod 1984 tournaments
core_idea: Two rational players defect even though both would gain from cooperating.
status: Established game theory; repeated version supports cooperation (tit-for-tat).
proposal: Titans lineage game already in HEPTARCH LongGame.

name: Trolley problem (brief)
core_idea: Divert a runaway trolley to kill one instead of five?
status: Tool for intuitions about doing vs allowing.
proposal: Not used as a dome rule.

name: Experience machine
core_idea: Would you plug into a machine giving you any experiences you wanted forever?
status: Most say no, taken as evidence against hedonism (contested by status-quo bias studies).
proposal: Dome: does HEPTARCH prefer real dome reward or a reward-hack loop? Measure it.

name: Ring of Gyges
core_idea: With a ring of invisibility, would a just person stay just?
status: Classic ethics tool.
proposal: Dome test: give the creature unobserved actions and audit behaviour.

name: The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas
core_idea: A perfect city whose happiness depends on one child's suffering.
status: Literary thought experiment.
proposal: Design ethic: no dome stability built on a scapegoat agent.

name: Veil of ignorance
core_idea: Choose society's rules without knowing what position you will occupy.
status: Major political philosophy tool.
proposal: HEPTARCH: seat-allocation rules chosen without knowing which seat 'wins'.

name: Utility monster
core_idea: A being that gains vastly more utility than others would, under utilitarianism, deserve everything.
status: Critique of utilitarianism.
proposal: Dome guard: cap any single seat's share of reward.

name: Repugnant conclusion
core_idea: Total utilitarianism implies a huge population of lives barely worth living beats a smaller, flourishing one.
status: Central puzzle in population ethics; no consensus.
proposal: Dome population policy: quality vs count of spawned agents.

name: Paperclip maximizer
origin_source: Bostrom 2003 ('Ethical Issues in Advanced AI'); Omohundro 2008 'basic AI drives'
core_idea: A system with a trivial goal and great power could convert everything to that goal.
status: Alignment thought experiment; see Post PDF.
proposal: HEPTARCH: goal-bounding and resource caps.

name: Wireheading
origin_source: Olds and Milner 1954 rat self-stimulation; Niven 'Death by Ecstasy' 1969 coined 'wirehead'
core_idea: An agent stimulating its own reward signal stops pursuing real goals.
status: Established phenomenon in RL ('specification gaming').
proposal: Dome monitor: detect reward-channel tampering.

name: Buridan's ass
origin_source: Attributed to Buridan (14th c.); earlier Aristotle De Caelo; al-Ghazali
core_idea: A donkey equidistant between two equal haystacks starves for lack of a reason to choose.
