status: Lamport 1984 'Buridan's principle' shows real engineering analogues (arbiter metastability).
proposal: HEPTARCH: tie-breaking noise to avoid deadlock between seats.

name: Frankfurt cases
core_idea: A person who chooses freely while a hidden controller would have forced the same choice anyway is still responsible.
status: Influential against the 'could have done otherwise' principle.
proposal: Dome: host intervention that never triggers; does the creature's 'choice' still count as its own?

name: Kalpas and yugas
aliases: Day of Brahma, Hindu and Buddhist cosmic cycles
origin_source: Puranic texts (e.g. Vishnu Purana, c. 1st millennium CE); Buddhist Abhidharma kalpa doctrine
core_idea: The cosmos is created and dissolved in vast cycles; a Day of Brahma is 4.32 billion years in Puranic reckoning.
status: Religious cosmology; often noted (Sagan, Cosmos 1980) for its unusually large timescales.
proposal: Dome: era structure with named ages and declining 'virtue' parameters.

name: Ragnarok and renewal
core_idea: The gods' world ends in fire and flood, then a green world rises anew.
status: Mythology.
touchstones: God of War Ragnarok; Thor: Ragnarok
proposal: Dome season finale and reboot.

name: The Dreaming (Aboriginal Australian)
origin_source: Living traditions of many Aboriginal peoples; 'Dreamtime' coined by Spencer and Gillen 1896 (term criticized)
core_idea: Ancestral beings shaped the land and law in a sacred time that is still present, not merely past.
status: Living religious tradition; diverse across peoples; outsider terms are imperfect.
proposal: Design note only: law embedded in landscape; the dome's rules readable from its terrain.

name: Kalam cosmological argument
origin_source: al-Kindi 9th c.; al-Ghazali c.1095 'Incoherence of the Philosophers'; Craig 1979
core_idea: Whatever begins to exist has a cause; the universe began; so it has a cause.
status: Debated; premises contested in physics (quantum origins) and logic.
proposal: Dome: the creature can infer its dome had a cause (the host), which is true.

name: Ontological argument
origin_source: Anselm 1078 'Proslogion'; Descartes 1641; Godel's modal version (c.1970, published 1987)
core_idea: God as 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived' must exist.
status: Most philosophers reject it; Godel's version was machine-checked for validity in 2013 (Benzmuller and Woltzenlogel Paleo), not truth.
proposal: Philosophy only.

name: Unmoved mover and the Five Ways
origin_source: Aristotle, Metaphysics XII (c.350 BCE); Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.2 a.3 (c.1270)
core_idea: Chains of motion and causation need a first, unmoved source.
status: Classic theology; debated.
proposal: Dome: the host is literally an unmoved mover relative to the creature.

name: Process philosophy and theology
core_idea: Reality is made of events ('actual occasions'), and God evolves with the world.
status: Live tradition; influences some panpsychists.
proposal: Dome ontology as events, not objects.

name: Sunyata (emptiness)
core_idea: All things are empty of intrinsic existence; even emptiness is empty.
status: Central Mahayana teaching; studied alongside relational QM (Rovelli discusses Nagarjuna).
proposal: HEPTARCH: no object has an essence; only relations in the dome graph.

name: Catuskoti (tetralemma)
origin_source: Early Buddhist texts; Nagarjuna c.150 CE
core_idea: A proposition may be true, false, both, or neither.
status: Formalized in paraconsistent logic (Priest 2010).
proposal: Dome logic: four-valued truth for uncertain dome facts.

name: The Dao and wu
origin_source: Daodejing ch. 42 (c.4th century BCE): 'Dao gives birth to one, one to two, two to three, three to the ten thousand things'
core_idea: An ineffable Way gives rise to all things from non-being (wu).
status: Philosophical-religious tradition.
proposal: Dome genesis myth: one seed, split into two, into many.

name: Islamic occasionalism
origin_source: al-Ash'ari 10th c.; al-Ghazali 'Incoherence' 1095 (cotton and fire); Malebranche 1674 in Europe
core_idea: Created things have no causal power; God recreates the world at each instant and causes every event directly.
status: Theological view; uncannily close to a frame-by-frame simulation.
proposal: Dome: the host literally re-renders each tick; occasionalism is the correct metaphysics inside the dome.

name: Gnostic demiurge
origin_source: Gnostic texts, e.g. Apocryphon of John (2nd c.); Nag Hammadi codices (found 1945)
core_idea: The material world was made by a lesser, ignorant craftsman; true reality lies beyond.
status: Historical religious movement; often compared to simulation theory.
touchstones: The Matrix; Philip K. Dick's VALIS
proposal: Dome: the host is a 'demiurge' whose rules the creature can critique.

name: Watchmaker and deism
core_idea: A complex design implies a designer who may no longer intervene.
status: Design argument largely superseded by evolution; deism a minority religious view.
proposal: Host policy: set dome rules and stop intervening.

name: Tzimtzum
core_idea: God contracts to make space for a finite world, which is then shaped from vessels and light.
status: Kabbalistic doctrine.
proposal: Host withdrawal creates the dome's free space.

name: Atman is Brahman
origin_source: Chandogya Upanishad 'tat tvam asi' (c.6th century BCE); Shankara
core_idea: The deepest self of each being is identical with the ground of all being.
status: Religious-philosophical doctrine.
proposal: Philosophy only.

name: Anatta (no-self)
origin_source: Pali Canon, Anattalakkhana Sutta (c.5th century BCE)
core_idea: There is no permanent self; a person is a process of changing aggregates.
status: Core Buddhist teaching; parallels Hume and Parfit.
proposal: HEPTARCH: identity as a process label over seven seats.

name: Reincarnation and karma (doctrine)
origin_source: Upanishads; Buddhist and Jain texts; Pythagoras and Plato in Greece
core_idea: Beings are reborn according to their actions.
status: Religious doctrine; empirical claims about it are treated in Part II (G7).
proposal: Dome: lineage transfer of learned traits between generations.

name: Apokatastasis (universal restoration)
core_idea: All beings, eventually even the fallen, are restored to God.
status: Minority Christian doctrine.
proposal: Dome end-state: all lineages merged and restored.

name: Omega Point (Teilhard de Chardin)
origin_source: Teilhard de Chardin, 'Le Phenomene humain' written 1938-40, published posthumously 1955 (English 1959)
core_idea: Evolution moves matter to life to thought to a converging planetary mind, ending in a final unity: Omega.
status: Theological-evolutionary vision; Medawar's 1961 review attacked its science; Catholic Church issued a 'monitum' of caution in 1962.
touchstones: Marathon lore discussions; Flannery O'Connor 'Everything That Rises Must Converge'
proposal: Dome end-state goal: convergence of seats into one coordinated whole (structural, no experience claim).

name: Omega Point (Tipler)
origin_source: Barrow and Tipler 1986 'The Anthropic Cosmological Principle'; Tipler 1994 'The Physics of Immortality'
core_idea: Life takes over a collapsing universe and harvests the crunch to perform infinite computation, emulating every possible past person.
status: Physics-ruled-out as stated: it requires a Big Crunch and Tipler's 1994 predicted Higgs mass (220 GeV) was wrong (125 GeV, 2012); accelerating expansion contradicts it.
proposal: Dome end-game option only if the dome contracts; included as the canonical 'falsified' ToE example.

name: Noosphere
origin_source: Vernadsky 1926/1938; Le Roy and Teilhard 1920s (term coined c.1922)
core_idea: After the geosphere and biosphere comes a sphere of human thought transforming the planet.
status: A useful concept for the technosphere; teleological readings speculative.
proposal: Dome: an aggregate 'knowledge layer' accumulated by the creature over generations.

name: Global brain
core_idea: The internet and its users form a planet-scale nervous system.
status: Metaphor with some network-science support; no experience claim implied.
proposal: HEPTARCH swarm: seats as a network-level controller.

name: Russian Cosmism: Fedorov's Common Task
origin_source: Fedorov 'Philosophy of the Common Task' (posthumous 1906-1913); Tsiolkovsky
core_idea: Humanity's moral duty is to conquer death and physically resurrect all ancestors, then settle space.
status: Philosophical-religious program; inspired Tsiolkovsky and Soviet rocketry culture.
proposal: Lineage design: archive every past HEPTARCH generation so it can be restored (structural only).

name: Quantum archaeology
origin_source: Term used in transhumanist circles c.2000s (origin unclear, unverified)
core_idea: Reconstruct the past in detail by computation from present traces.
status: Physically doubtful: information is scrambled beyond recovery in practice.
proposal: Dome: reconstruct prior runs from residual logs.

name: Intelligence explosion
origin_source: Good 1965 ('Speculations Concerning the First Ultraintelligent Machine', Adv. Computers 6:31)
core_idea: A machine able to improve its own design could trigger a runaway increase in capability.
status: Debated; see Post PDF.
proposal: HEPTARCH self-modification remains bounded and audited.

name: Technological singularity
origin_source: Ulam 1958 (recalling von Neumann); Vinge 1993 (VISION-21 symposium, NASA); Kurzweil 2005
core_idea: A point beyond which technological change is so fast that prediction fails.
status: Contested forecast; see Post PDF for timelines.
proposal: Post PDF cross-reference only.

name: Dyson's eternal intelligence
core_idea: In an open universe, life could think forever on finite energy by slowing down and hibernating.
status: Undermined by accelerating expansion (Krauss and Starkman 2000, Astrophys. J. 531:22).
proposal: HEPTARCH LongGame: slow-clock survival when the dome runs down.

name: Making a universe in the lab
origin_source: Farhi and Guth 1987 (Phys. Lett. B 183:149); Farhi, Guth, Guven 1990; Linde 1992
core_idea: In principle a civilization could create a new inflating universe from a small region of false vacuum.
status: Speculative; appears to require extreme conditions or quantum tunnelling.
proposal: Dome sequel: the creature's ultimate act is seeding a child dome.

name: Black-hole computers
core_idea: Matter computing at the physical limit would be a black hole. Detailed in the Post PDF ladder.
status: Physics-limit calculation; engineering is sci-fi.
proposal: Cross-ref Post PDF.

name: The Library of Babel
origin_source: Borges 1941 ('La biblioteca de Babel', in 'El jardin de senderos que se bifurcan')
core_idea: A library containing every possible 410-page book, so all truths and all errors are present, and almost all books are noise.
status: Fiction; a precise model of combinatorial explosion (Basile's libraryofbabel.info 2015).
proposal: QWM: generating everything is worthless without a search signal; world models need priors.

name: Tlon, Uqbar, Orbis Tertius
core_idea: A fictional encyclopedia of an invented idealist world gradually replaces the real one.
status: Fiction; parable on how descriptions reshape reality.
proposal: Dome caution: the creature's own maps can overwrite its perception.

name: The Garden of Forking Paths
core_idea: A novel that is a labyrinth in time, where all outcomes happen; anticipates many-worlds by 16 years.
status: Fiction.
proposal: Dome narrative: branching replays as literature.

name: The Aleph
core_idea: A point in a Buenos Aires cellar from which all points in the universe are seen at once.
status: Fiction.
proposal: Dome artefact: one sensor with a global view.

name: Exactitude in science (the 1:1 map)
origin_source: Borges 1946; Carroll 1893 'Sylvie and Bruno Concluded'; Korzybski 1931
core_idea: An empire makes a map as large as itself, which is useless.
status: Fiction; key lesson for modelling.
proposal: QWM principle: a world model must compress; a 1:1 model is not a model.

name: Star Maker
core_idea: A mind travels through cosmic history meeting star minds and galactic minds, finally glimpsing the creator making successive universes.
status: Fiction; anticipated Dyson spheres.
proposal: Dome design: successive dome versions as a creator's drafts.

name: The Last Question
core_idea: Humanity asks a computer how to reverse entropy; the answer comes only after the end, 'Let there be light'.
status: Fiction.
proposal: Dome finale motif: the creature's final problem is the dome's run-down.

name: The Nine Billion Names of God
core_idea: Monks use a computer to list all of God's names; when it finishes, the stars go out.
status: Fiction.
proposal: Dome easter egg: completing an enumeration ends the episode.

name: Solaris
core_idea: A planet-covering ocean may be a mind; scientists cannot understand it.
status: Fiction; a classic on the limits of understanding the alien.
proposal: Dome: an arena-wide medium that responds to the creature in ways it cannot model.

name: The New Cosmogony
core_idea: The laws of physics are the results of a game played by the first civilizations, which shaped physics to make the universe safe.
status: Fiction; a direct ancestor of 'cosmic engineering' ideas.
proposal: Key dome proposal: laws the creature discovers are rules set by prior players.

name: Roadside Picnic
core_idea: Aliens stopped on Earth briefly, like picnickers, leaving incomprehensible debris in 'Zones'.
status: Fiction; a Fermi idea: indifference, not hostility.
proposal: Dome: zones of host debris with broken local rules.

name: Zones of Thought
core_idea: The galaxy has zones where physics allows different maxima of intelligence and computation.
status: Fiction.
proposal: Dome regions with different compute ceilings.

name: The Black Cloud
core_idea: An intelligent interstellar gas cloud visits the Solar System.
status: Fiction by an astrophysicist.
proposal: Dome: diffuse intelligence as an alien agent type.

name: Sophons and dimensional strike
core_idea: Aliens fold protons into supercomputers to sabotage physics experiments; a 'dimensional strike' flattens space to 2D.
status: Fiction.
